In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-Nahl

It is Meccan except for the last three verses, namely His words, exalted is He: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished﴾ to the end of the surah. It is also said that His words ﴿Then indeed your Lord, for those who emigrated after they had been tried...﴾ and the verse are Medinan as well. This surah is called Surat al-Ni'am (the Surah of Blessings), and it is also said to be called Surat al-Ala' (the Surah of Favours).

His words, exalted is He: ﴿The command of Allah has come﴾, meaning: it has drawn near and approached, like a man saying to another, "The news has come to you" or "The aid has come to you" when it has drawn near to him. It is also said that its meaning is "The command of Allah will come," just as one says, "If you honour me, I will honour you," meaning, "I will honour you." They differed regarding the meaning of His words ﴿the command of Allah﴾. The majority hold that what is meant by it is His punishment and His chastisement of the deniers who reject.

The second view: that what is meant by the command of Allah is the obligations and the rulings. This is reported from al-Dahhak, and it is a weak view. Al-Kalbi and others claimed that what is meant by it is the Resurrection.

His words ﴿So do not seek to hasten it﴾: al-istti'jal (hastening) is seeking a thing before its time. Its meaning is: do not seek it before its time. It is narrated from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: When the words ﴿The command of Allah has come﴾ were revealed, the disbelievers raised their heads and thought that it had truly come; when He said ﴿So do not seek to hasten it﴾, they lowered their heads. In some reports: "When the words of Allah, exalted is He, ﴿The command of Allah has come﴾ were revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up in alarm, and Jibril said: ﴿So do not seek to hasten it﴾." Muqatil has mentioned this in his tafsir.

His words ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾ mean: He is exalted, by His praiseworthy attributes, above what the polytheists describe Him with.

The Speech of Allah, the Exalted: "He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command" (Qur'an 16:2). Mujahid narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that the Spirit (al-Ruh) is a creation of Allah, the Exalted, in the forms of the children of Adam, and they are not angels. Allah does not send down any angel except that with him is a Spirit. The second view is that the Spirit is the revelation (al-wahy), because by it the life of the hearts is achieved, just as by the spirit the life of the bodies is achieved. It was also said that it is prophethood (al-nubuwwah), and it was said that it is mercy (al-rahmah).

As for His saying: "upon whomever He wills of His servants" (Qur'an 16:2), it means: from among the Prophets and the Messengers.

As for His saying: "that you warn that there is no god but I, so fear Me" (Qur'an 16:2), its meaning is: command them to say "there is no god but Allah," warning and threatening them with the punishment, whether they say it or not. Then His saying "so fear Me" means: fear Me.

The words of the Most High: ﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth﴾, meaning: to manifest the truth. And the words of the Most High: ﴿Exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾, meaning: He is exalted above what they associate with Him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 4:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿He created man from a drop of fluid﴾. It is said that this verse was revealed concerning Ubayy ibn Khalaf, but the sound view is that it is general, applying to everyone. And His words: ﴿then behold, he becomes a clear adversary﴾, meaning: a disputer who openly expresses what is in his heart through contention. Contention (khusumah) may be praiseworthy and may be blameworthy. The praiseworthy kind is that which is aimed at making the truth manifest, and the blameworthy kind is that which is aimed at repelling the truth. The meaning of the verse is a demonstration of power, namely that God, exalted is He, created the drop from something in this state. It is also said that the purpose of the verse is to demonstrate blessing. And it is said that the purpose of the verse is to expose the ugliness of their deeds in denying God's blessing while it was manifest to them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the cattle — He created them for you; in them is warmth (dif')⁠﴾. Al-dafʾ is the moderate heat that is found in the body of a person from the covering (al-dithar). As for the meaning of the verse: Ibn ʿAbbas said: al-dafʾ is clothing. Qatadah said: it is what one warms oneself with of wool and fur, and what is similar to that.

Some of them said: al-dafʾ is offspring (al-nasl), and al-Amidi mentioned that this is from the speech of the Arabs.

His saying: ﴿and benefits﴾. Al-manafiʿ (benefits) are riding and offspring-bearing, and all else from which one benefits. His saying: ﴿and from them you eat﴾ is the taking of their meat and their milk.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 6:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And for you in them there is beauty﴾, meaning adornment. Al-Suddi said: "The beauty (al-jamal) is that when they go out and are seen, it is said: 'These are the camels of so-and-so.'"

As for His specifying, ﴿when you bring them home in the evening and when you send them out to pasture﴾: the "rawah" (evening return) regarding livestock is when they come back from their grazing lands to their owners' enclosures in the evening, and the "sarah" (morning departure) is when they leave the enclosures for the pastures in the morning. If someone asks: why was "rawah" mentioned first, when "sarah" is the one that comes first? We say: because the owner takes more pride in them when they return (in the evening), and because the benefits from them are mainly taken after the return.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 7:

And His saying: ﴿and they carry your loads﴾. Al-thiql (the burden) is the goods whose carrying is heavy. And His saying: ﴿to a land you could not have reached except with great hardship to yourselves﴾, meaning: with the effort of your selves and their toil. It has been recited as "bi-shiqq al-anfus" (with the strain of the souls). The scholars differed concerning the land mentioned. Some of them said it is Makkah, and some said it is any land in the world. If someone says: what hardship is there in riding an animal that is tame and gentle and traveling on it from one land to another, with complete provisions and safety of the road?

The answer: travel is not free of hardship in general. And the second answer: the meaning of the verse is that you could not have reached it except with great hardship to yourselves, were it not for these animals.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful﴾ — its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 16, verse 8:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And horses, mules, and donkeys﴾ – the verse. It is related that Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' was asked: "Why were horses called khayl?" He did not mention anything, and there was a Bedouin present, who said: "Horses were called khayl because of their strutting (ikhtiyal)."

As for His saying: ﴿that you may ride them﴾, some have claimed that riding the red donkeys, the fine ones, is more eloquent in adornment than riding horses and mules, because God Exalted said: ﴿that you may ride them and as adornment﴾ following the mention of donkeys. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They said, "Call upon your Lord for us to bring forth for us from what the earth grows – of its herbs, its cucumbers, its garlic, its lentils, and its onions."﴾ This shows that onions are baser than these things, since He mentioned ﴿Would you exchange that which is lower for that which is better?﴾ following the mention of onions. It has also been said: the worst donkeys are the black, short ones.

The more preferable view is that beauty is greater in horses, for their handsomeness and visibility, and because God Exalted began with them in mention.

It was said to Khalid ibn Safwan: "Why do you not ride donkeys?" He said: "They are slow in relief and abundant in dung; when they travel they are slow, and when they stop they release." He was once seen on a donkey, and was asked about that, and he said: "I discipline it with a gentle pace, and I throw to it a little grain, and it prevents me from being a tyrannical, obstinate man."

It is established that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) rode a horse, a mule, and a donkey. In the reports: the prophets of the Children of Israel used to ride she-asses. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he disliked eating horse meat; he said: "Because God Exalted said: ﴿that you may ride them and as adornment﴾." But it is established through the narration of Jabir that the Prophet (ﷺ) permitted the flesh of horses, and it is also established from Asma' bint Abi Bakr al-Siddiq that she said: "We ate horse meat in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)." Therefore the preferable ruling is permissibility, and most scholars hold it.

As for His saying: ﴿and He creates what you do not know﴾, it has been said its meaning is: He creates what does not occur to anyone's mind, for a person rarely passes a day and a night without seeing something of God's creation that he had not seen before. Ibn al-Suddi related from his father that the meaning of His saying ﴿and He creates what you do not know﴾ is: the weevil in plants and grains. And in some tafsirs it is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning this verse: "Indeed God has a white earth which He created, its expanse being the distance the sun travels in thirty nights, and He has filled it with creation that has never disobeyed God for the blink of an eye." It was said to him: "Are they from the children of Adam?" He said: "They do not know that God created Adam." It was said to him: "How then does Iblis not tempt them?" He said: "They do not know that God has in His creation Iblis." This report is strange, and God knows best.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 9:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾. It is said that its meaning is: upon Allah is the explanation of guidance from error. It is also said: the explanation of the truth through the signs and proofs, and this is by way of a promise. And it is said: ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾, i.e., upon Allah is judging with justice among the creatures.

And His words: ﴿And of it is one that deviates﴾. Its meaning: and of the way is one that deviates. ʿAlī and Ibn Masʿūd recited: "And among you is one that deviates" (wa-minkum jāʾir). I.e., one who swerves away from the truth. The poet said:

(When our blood was mixed with their blood... the heavy-laden stood by it, and the just one (wa-jār) deviated.)

Al-thiqāl: the insolent (al-biṭar).

And His words: ﴿And had He willed, He would have guided you all﴾. The meaning is clear, and in it is a refutation of the Qadariyya.

Almighty God's saying: ﴿It is He who sends down water from the sky; from it you have drink﴾. That is: from it you have what you drink.

And His saying: ﴿And from it are trees in which you pasture [your livestock]﴾. That is: you pasture the livestock in them, and al-isāmah (pasturing) is letting the livestock loose to graze.

And the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿He causes to grow for you thereby the crops, the olives, the date palms, the grapes, and of every kind of fruit. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought.﴾ and the verse [continues]. Its meaning is apparent.

God Most High says: ﴿And He has made subservient to you the night and the day﴾, meaning: He has made the night and the day subservient to you (dhallala lakum). It has also been said: He made the light of the sun subservient for the day and the light of the moon for the night.

His saying: ﴿And the stars are made subservient by His command﴾, meaning: made subservient (mudhallalat) by His command. His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for a people who reason﴾, its meaning is apparent.

﴿And what He has created for you on the earth⁠﴾, i.e., what He has created for you on the earth. And His words, ﴿of differing colors⁠﴾, i.e., its form and its appearance. And His words, ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for a people who remember⁠﴾, i.e., who reflect.

He it is who subjected the sea, that you may eat from it fresh flesh, i.e., fish; and that you may extract from it ornaments to wear. And it says: "You may extract from it ornaments which you wear," meaning pearls that you make into adornment.

And His saying: ﴿And you see the ships ploughing through it﴾. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Mawaqir" — i.e., laden, filled. It is also said: "Mawakhir" means advancing and retreating with one wind. The makhr is the cleaving; a ship "tamkhur al-ma'" means it cleaves the water. In a report it is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When one of you wants to urinate, let him make his makhr with the wind" — i.e., let him look at the place from which it blows and turn his back to it. The makhr is also the sound of the wind at its strongest.

And His saying: ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾, meaning: for trade. And His saying: ﴿so that perhaps you will be grateful﴾, meaning: when you see God's craftsmanship in what He has subjected for you.

It is narrated that ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) wrote to ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs asking him about the sea. He replied: "It is a great creature which a weak creature rides, worms on a piece of wood, with nothing but sky and water. If it leans, it drowns; if it survives, it is bewildered" — i.e., astonished and perplexed.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 15:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And He cast into the earth firm mountains﴾, meaning: fixed mountains. And in the reports (al-athar) it is related that when Allah the Most High created the earth, it used to tilt and sway; so the angels said: "Indeed, this earth will not settle with anyone upon its back." Then, in the morning, they found that He had created the mountains, and it became stable and firm.

And His words: ﴿lest it should shake with you﴾, meaning: lest it should incline with you. And His words: ﴿and rivers and roads﴾, meaning: paths. And His words: ﴿that you may be guided﴾, meaning: that you may be guided by the road and the mountains.

And His saying: ﴿and landmarks﴾, meaning: and indications. It has also been said that these landmarks are the mountains. And His saying: ﴿and by the star they are guided﴾. Al-Farra' said: "By the Little Bear (al-Jadi) and the two Guards (al-Farqadan)." It has also been said: "and by the stars they are guided." And on the authority of Qatadah, who said: "Allah created the stars for three things: as an adornment for the lowest heaven, as missiles against the devils, and to be guided by them on the sea and on land. Whoever seeks from them knowledge other than this has erred. And these three things are mentioned in the Qur'an."

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Is then He who creates like one who does not create?﴾ It was said: meaning, "Is then He who bestows blessings like one who does not bestow blessings?" And His saying: ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ means: will you not then take heed?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 18:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate it﴾. That is, you would not be able to count it. It has also been said: you would not be able to thank Him for it. As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, its meaning is apparent.

Almighty God's saying: ﴿And God knows what you conceal and what you disclose. And those whom they invoke besides God create nothing, and they are created.﴾ He meant by this the idols. And His saying: ﴿and they are created﴾ means: that which is created cannot be a god.

Almighty God's saying: ﴿And God knows what you conceal and what you disclose. And those whom they invoke besides God create nothing, and they are created.﴾ He meant by this the idols. And His saying: ﴿and they are created﴾ means: that which is created cannot be a god.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 21:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Dead, not alive﴾. If it is said: how can an idol be dead when it has never been alive? The answer: its meaning is that they are like the dead in that they do not understand.

And His words: ﴿not alive﴾ are an emphasis of the first. And His words: ﴿And they do not perceive when they will be raised﴾, meaning: when will they be raised? If it is said: do the idols have a resurrection? The answer: it has been mentioned in some tafsirs that the idols will be raised, and life will be placed in them, and they will disavow their worshippers, and the Qur'an has indicated this in several places. And it has been said regarding the meaning of the verse: "And the idols do not perceive when the disbelievers will be raised?" And there is a third opinion regarding the verse: its meaning is: "And the disbelievers do not perceive when they will be raised?"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 22:

The words of God Most High: ﴿Your God is one God. As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, their hearts are denying, and they are arrogant.﴾ That is: their hearts are denying (jahida). This is evidence that what counts is the denial and rejection of the heart.

And His words: ﴿And they are arrogant (mustakbirun).﴾ That is: they are proud (mutakabbirun). It is said: no one denies the religion except a proud person.

God Most High said: ﴿Indeed, when it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," they were arrogant (yastakbirun).﴾ And it has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "No one will enter Paradise who has in his heart an atom's weight of pride."
Allah the Exalted's saying: ﴿Without doubt﴾ its meaning is: truly. {Indeed, Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He does not love the arrogant}, meaning: the proud.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 24:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when it is said to them, "What has your Lord sent down?"﴾ its meaning: And when it is said to the disbelievers mentioned earlier, "What has your Lord sent down?" What is it that your Lord has sent down?

And His saying: ﴿They say, "Tales of the former peoples."﴾ It means: lies of the former peoples. The word "asatir" (plural of usṭūrah, "tale" or "fable") is the plural of usṭūrah, and it is said: stories of the former peoples.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 25:

And His saying: ﴿And that they will bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection﴾. The "awzar" (burdens) are the sins (dhunub).

And His saying: ﴿in full﴾. He mentioned the fullness because the afflictions and trials that befall them in this world do not expiate any of their sins, and likewise what they do intending good deeds.

And His saying: ﴿and some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge﴾. That is, some of the sins of those whom they mislead, who are their followers.

If someone says: How can they bear the burdens of the followers, when God, exalted is He, says: ﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾? The answer to this is: they bear their sins by way of the incitement and the calling to error, for it has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever calls to guidance and is followed, he will have its reward and the reward of whoever acts upon it until the Day of Resurrection, without any diminution of their rewards. And whoever calls to misguidance and is followed, upon him is its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it until the Day of Resurrection, without any diminution of their burdens."

﴿Those before them had already plotted, so God came at their structures from the foundations, and the roof fell down upon them from above them﴾.

And His saying: ﴿without knowledge﴾ means: they returned to mere blind imitation (taqlid) without evidence. Some of them said its meaning is: they called them to error without proof. And His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they bear﴾ means: unquestionably, wretched is what they carry of sins.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 26:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those before them had already plotted﴾. Its meaning: those before them had already associated partners with God (ashraka). It has also been said: makr (plotting) is corrupt planning.

And His saying: ﴿So God came at their structure from its foundations﴾. This is mentioned in the manner of a parable, meaning: God uprooted their plotting from its root and turned the consequence and harm of their plotting back upon them. Otherwise there was no structure, no foundation and no roof.

The second view regarding the verse: the verse was revealed concerning Nimrod ibn Kan'an when he built the tower (al-sarh) to ascend to heaven. In the narration: he built a palace whose height into the sky was two farsakhs, and it was said: it was five thousand dhira' and a little more, and its width was three thousand dhira'. So God sent Jibril (peace be upon him), who struck its top into the sea, then demolished the rest. It fell upon them while they were beneath it. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So God came at their structure from its foundations, and the roof fell down upon them from above them﴾. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas (may God be pleased with them both).

If it is said: He said, ﴿the roof fell down upon them from above them﴾; what is the meaning of His saying ﴿from above them﴾, when the meaning has already been understood from His saying ﴿the roof fell down upon them﴾? The answer: this is mentioned for emphasis, like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾, and like His saying: ﴿So woe to those who write the Book with their own hands﴾.

Another answer, mentioned by Ibn al-Anbari and others: the Arabs say "kharra 'ala fulan bayutuhu" (his houses fell upon so-and-so) when they collapse, even if he was not beneath them. When they say "kharra 'ala fulan baytuhu min fawqihi" (his house fell upon him from above him), it is understood that he was beneath it. His saying: ﴿and the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive﴾ means: from the direction in which they had felt secure.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 27:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them﴾, meaning: He will humiliate them and degrade them therein. And His saying: ﴿and He will say, "Where are My partners, whom you used to oppose [them]?"﴾, meaning: whom you used to oppose (tu'adduna, تعادون) the believers concerning them.

If it is said: "Where are My partners?" when God has no partner, how is the meaning of the verse? The answer is that its meaning is: "Where are My partners in your claim?" ﴿And among them is one who says, "Where are those whom you used to claim as partners?"﴾

And His saying: ﴿Those who were given knowledge will say﴾, meaning: the believers.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, disgrace today and evil are upon the disbelievers﴾, its meaning: that the punishment today and the humiliation are upon the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 28:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves﴾. The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: this was revealed concerning a people who embraced Islam in Makkah, but when the Prophet emigrated, they did not emigrate. Then, when the polytheists went out to Badr, they took them along with themselves. When they saw the Prophet and the small number of those with him, they thought they would be destroyed at the hands of the polytheists. So they remained with the disbelievers, and they were killed that day. Then God, exalted is He, revealed concerning them this verse: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves﴾. Its meaning: in the state of their wronging themselves by abandoning emigration with the Prophet and going out with the disbelievers.

His statement: ﴿So they will offer submission﴾, meaning: they submitted and yielded to the Angel of Death.

And His statement: ﴿We did not do any evil﴾, meaning: we were not polytheists. And His statement: ﴿Yes, indeed, Allah is Knowing of what you used to do﴾, meaning: Allah knows that you did the deeds of the disbelievers, and the deed of the disbelievers is abandoning emigration and going out with the polytheists. At the beginning of Islam, Islam was not accepted except together with emigration (hijrah), so these people embraced Islam but did not emigrate, and therefore their Islam was not accepted.

Qur'anic quotations: ﴿فادخلوا أَبْوَاب جَهَنَّم خَالِدين فِيهَا﴾ and ﴿فلبئس مثوى المتكبرين﴾.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿So enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ means: remaining there eternally. Here there is an implied element (idmar), namely that it is said to them: "Enter the gates of Hell." And His saying: ﴿How wretched is the abode of the arrogant﴾ means: the dwelling place of the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it will be said to those who feared God, "What has your Lord sent down?"﴾ If it is said: He had earlier said, ﴿And when it is said to them, "What has your Lord sent down?" they say, "Legends of the former peoples,"﴾ with the nominative (marfu') case, and here He says, ﴿"What has your Lord sent down?" They say, "Good."﴾ with the accusative (mansub) case. How then are the two verses to be understood?

The answer: The meaning of His saying, ﴿Legends of the former peoples,﴾ is: what was sent down is legends of the former peoples. And His saying, ﴿They say, "Good,"﴾ means: our Lord has sent down good. And His saying, ﴿For those who did good in this world there is good,﴾ their doing good is the statement: there is no god but God. And His saying, ﴿good (hasanah),﴾ its meaning has been disputed:

Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the multiplication of the reward up to tenfold and beyond. Al-Dahhak said: the hasanah is victory and conquest. Mujahid said: it is good provision. Others said: it is what God opened to the Muslims of the lands and the spoils of war He bestowed upon them.

His saying, ﴿And the abode of the Hereafter is better,﴾ means: and the state of the abode of the Hereafter is better.

His saying, ﴿And how excellent is the abode of the God-fearing,﴾ most of the exegetes hold that what is meant by it is Paradise. It is related from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said: it is this world, and this world is the abode of the God-fearing, from it one provisions oneself for the Hereafter, and in it the pleasure of God, exalted is He, is sought. It is related from 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, that when he distributed gifts between the Emigrants (muhajirun) and the Helpers (ansar) he would say: "This is for you in this world, and what God has stored up for you in the Hereafter."
The Most High's saying: ﴿Gardens of Eden, which they will enter, with rivers flowing beneath them. For them therein is whatever they wish. Thus God rewards the righteous.﴾ Clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 32:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are good﴾, meaning: pure, purified from polytheism (shirk). It was also said: its meaning is that their death occurs in a good and easy manner.

His saying: ﴿They will say, "Peace be upon you"﴾. It is said that what is meant by this is the greeting of the angels, who convey to them the peace of Allah. And in the reports: "They say to each one of them, 'Peace be upon you, O friend of Allah.'" And from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: the believing deceased is escorted to Allah just as a bride is escorted. And His saying: ﴿Enter Paradise for what you used to do﴾, meaning: it will be said to them, "Enter Paradise by your faith and your obedience."

"The word of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them?﴾ Its meaning: Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them with death? ﴿Or that the command of your Lord should come?﴾ That is the Resurrection.

It is related in some reports that the assistants of the Angel of Death are six angels: three who seize the souls of the believers, and three who seize the souls of the disbelievers. It is also said: ﴿Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them﴾ with punishment and killing for the disbelievers, ﴿or that the command of your Lord should come?﴾ That is, death. And His word: ﴿Thus did those before them do﴾ means: thus did those who were before them disbelieve. And His word: ﴿And Allah did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves﴾ — its meaning is apparent."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 34:

The saying of Allah Most High: ﴿So the evil consequences of what they had done befell them﴾ means: the calamity (wabal) of the evil deeds they had done befell them. It is also said: the recompense (jaza') for the evil deeds they had done. And His saying: ﴿and what they used to mock at encompassed them﴾ means: it descended upon them and surrounded them, that which they used to mock at.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 35:**

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who associated partners with God said, "Had God willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything apart from Him."﴾

The prohibition mentioned in the verse refers to what they forbade of the *bahira* (a she-camel whose ear was slit and set free), the *wasila* (a she-camel or sheep whose offspring was withheld from them), the *sa'iba* (a beast set free for their idols), and the *ham* (a stallion camel released after it had sired a certain number of offspring).

The Qadariyya (the school that affirms human power to create one's own actions and denies that God predetermines them) have used this verse as evidence. Their argument is that the polytheists said, "Had God willed, we would not have associated partners with Him, nor would our fathers, [﴿nor would we have forbidden anything apart from Him﴾]." Then God said at the end of the verse, ﴿Thus did those before them act﴾, as a rebuke and a denial against them. This shows, they argue, that God does not will disbelief, and that they did what they did without God's will.

The answer to this is that al-Zajjaj and others have mentioned that they said this statement in a mocking manner, not in earnest. Had they said it in earnest, their statement would have agreed with the statement of the believers. The same applies to God's words about the story of Shu'ayb: ﴿Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided﴾, for they said this in mockery, not in earnest. Likewise God's words in Surah Ya Sin: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Spend from what God has provided you," those who disbelieved say to those who believed, "Shall we feed one whom God, if He willed, would feed?"﴾ They said this only in mockery, because in itself it is a true statement that agrees with the statement of the believers. Likewise here, they said what they said in mockery, and therefore God denied it against them and rejected their statement. The evidence that this is what is meant is what is mentioned afterwards, and we will clarify it.

As for His words, ﴿So is there upon the messengers anything but clear notification?﴾, it means: guidance and misguidance are not up to them; rather, their duty is only to convey (the message).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 36:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We certainly sent among every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid the taghut"﴾. That is: affirm the oneness of Allah and avoid the idols.

His saying: ﴿So among them are those whom Allah guided, and among them are those upon whom error was made due﴾. Its meaning: among them are those whom Allah guided to faith, and among them are those upon whom error became obligatory, and He left them in disbelief by the preceding decree. So this verse makes clear that whoever believes does so by the will of Allah, and whoever disbelieves, disbelieves by the will of Allah.

His saying: ﴿So travel through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers﴾. Its meaning: the outcome and final destination of the matter of the deniers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 37:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you are eager for their guidance﴾. Al-hirs (eagerness) is seeking something with earnestness and striving.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide those who lead themselves astray﴾. He recited it in two readings. The people of Kufa recited: "lā yahdī man yuḍill" with a fatḥah on the first yā' and a ḍammah on the second, while the rest recited: "lā yahdī man yuḍill" with a ḍammah on both yā's. As for the first reading, its meaning is: Allah does not guide the one whom He has led astray. As for the second reading, its meaning is: indeed, the one whom Allah leads astray is not guided. It was also said: no one can have power over his guidance. They said: this is the better of the two readings.

And His saying: ﴿And for them there are no helpers﴾, meaning: those who would prevent them from the punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 38:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And they swear by Allah with their most emphatic oaths﴾. The "most emphatic oath" (jahd al-yamin) is that one swears by Allah, there is no god besides Him. And His words: ﴿Allah will not raise up one who dies﴾. This is evidence that they were clear-sighted in their disbelief.

And His words: ﴿Yes, it is a promise binding upon Him in truth﴾. Its meaning: the matter is not as they said, but rather Allah will resurrect them. Then He said: ﴿a promise binding upon Him in truth﴾, i.e., obligatory.

And His words: ﴿But most of mankind do not know﴾. It means: that the promise of Allah is true, for only the believers know it, not the disbelievers.

Almighty God's words: ﴿That He may make clear to them that about which they differ﴾ mean: that the truth may become manifest to them in what they differ about. And His words: ﴿and that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars﴾ mean: in the world.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 40:

The words of God, Exalted: ﴿Indeed, when We intend a thing and say to it, "Be," it is.﴾ If it is said: You have stated that the non-existent is not a thing, yet God has here called the non-existent a thing, saying: ﴿Indeed, Our word to a thing when We intend it﴾, and its meaning is: when We intend its bringing into being.

The answer: the things whose existence God has decreed are, in God's knowledge, like those that are already existing (al-qa'imah). Thus the statement ﴿Indeed, Our word to a thing when We intend it﴾ is sound. It has also been said that this is according to the figurative manner (tariq al-majaz), and its meaning is: it becomes a thing only when We intend its bringing into being.

As for His words ﴿that We say to it﴾, its meaning is: that We say to it for its sake (li-ajlihi): ﴿"Be," and it is.﴾ That is, "Be," and it was. It has been recited in two readings: "fayakun" with the accusative (fatha), and "wayakun" with the nominative (damma).

As for the nominative reading, its meaning is: so it is. As for the accusative reading, it is conjoined (manswaq) to His words ﴿that We say﴾, and that requires the accusative.

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And those who emigrated for the sake of Allah after they had been wronged﴾. The people of tafsir said: the verse was revealed concerning ʿAmmar, Bilal, Suhayb ibn Sinan, Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, and Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah. His saying ﴿after they had been wronged﴾ means: after they had been tortured and harmed.

His saying ﴿We will surely settle them in this world in a good place﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Shaʿbi and al-Hasan said: it is al-Madinah. It is also said: it is "the seat of truthfulness" (qadam al-sidq). And it was said: it is success (al-tawfiq) and guidance (al-hidayah).

His saying ﴿And the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew﴾. That is: greater, if only they knew. His saying ﴿if only they knew﴾ is directed at the polytheists, not at these particular men, for these men already knew that the reward of the Hereafter is greater."

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿Those who were patient and upon their Lord they rely﴾ is clear in meaning, and it was revealed concerning these five.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 43:

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed⦆ means: except men from among mankind to whom We revealed. For the polytheists used to deny that human beings were sent, and they demanded that angels be sent, as God the Exalted mentions this in more than one place. As for His statement: ﴿So ask the people of the Reminder⦆, it means: the believers among the People of the Book. It was also said: the bearers of the knowledge of the two Books, for they did not deny this. As for His statement: ﴿if you do not know⦆, its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 44:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿with the clear proofs and the scriptures﴾. The scholars differed concerning what the phrase ﴿with the clear proofs and the scriptures﴾ refers back to.

Some of them said its meaning is: "We did not send before you except men with the clear proofs and the scriptures." Others said its meaning is: "We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed with the clear proofs and the scriptures." Then He said: ﴿So ask the people of the Reminder, if you do not know﴾.

His saying: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder, that you may make clear to mankind what has been sent down to them﴾. The Messenger was an explainer of the revelation, and the people of knowledge have said: the explanation of the Book is in the Sunnah. His saying: ﴿and that they may reflect﴾ means: that they may ponder and take warning.

The words of Allah, Glorified and Exalted: ﴿Do those who have plotted evil deeds feel secure that Allah will cause the earth to swallow them?﴾ "Plotted evil deeds" means they committed evil deeds, namely their denial of monotheism (tawhid), their worship of other than Allah, and their acts of disobedience. Some have said that makr (plotting) in this context means striving for corruption, and what we have said is more corrupting of corruption.

As for His words, ﴿that Allah will cause the earth to swallow them﴾, al-khasf (the swallowing up by the earth) is a well-known meaning. It has been established from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "While a man was walking proudly in his garment, the earth swallowed him, and he will keep sinking into it until the Day of Resurrection."

Al-Naqqash related from some scholars, with a chain of narration, that a people contended for the leadership of the prayer after the iqamah had been called, and so Allah caused the earth to swallow them.

In some of the musnads, from Abu Hurayrah, the Prophet ﷺ said: "A mine will be opened for the people, and gold will appear from it like the camels of Bukht; the people will incline towards it, and Allah will cause them to be swallowed up along with the mine, and they will keep sinking into it until the Day of Resurrection."

As for His words, ﴿or that the punishment will come upon them from where they do not perceive﴾, this means: from where they do not know.

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Or He seizes them in their going to and fro﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: "In their coming and going." It was also said: "In their night and day." And it was said: "In their travels." And His saying: ﴿so they cannot escape﴾, meaning: they cannot get away (fa'ita, "outstrip"; fa'itin, "escaping").

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 47:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or He seizes them by gradual wasting?﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: "by gradual wasting (tanaqqus)." The meaning of tanaqqus here is that He seizes them one after another, the first and then the next, until He destroys them.

The second view: the meaning of takhawwuf (fear, apprehension) is that He seizes one people and does not seize others, and their apprehension is by the seizing of those. This is the view of al-Hasan and al-Dahhak.

The third view: it is related from al-Layth ibn Saʿd that he said: "I heard that it means 'with haste.'"

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful﴾. His mercy toward the disbelievers is their being granted respite in the punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 48:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not considered what things Allah has created, how their shadows turn about, [inclining] to the right and to the left, prostrating to Allah while they are humbled?﴾ (yatafayya'u zilaluhu) means: their shadows shift and turn. As for the difference between al-fay' (shadow after noon) and al-zill (shadow), it is said: al-zill is in the morning, and al-fay' is in the afternoon. It is also said that the two mean the same thing.

His saying: ﴿ʿan al-yamin﴾ (to the right) means "from the rights" (ʿan al-aymān), because He said immediately after it: ﴿wa al-shamaʾil﴾ (and to the left). The shadow revolves around the sides of a person: sometimes it is on his right, sometimes on his left, sometimes in front of him, and sometimes behind him.

His saying: ﴿sujjadan li-llah﴾ (prostrating to Allah). Most of the early scholars (al-salaf) held that prostration here means obedience to Allah, and that all things are prostrating to Allah, obedient, both animate and inanimate. This is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Hasan al-Basri. Al-Hasan said: "O son of Adam, your shadow prostrates to Allah, the Exalted, and you do not prostrate. How evil is what you have done."

Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi mentioned in his Jami', with a narration of Ibn ʿUmar from ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both), that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Four [units of prayer] after the decline of the sun before the Zuhr are equal to their like before dawn, and there is nothing that does not prostrate to Allah at that hour." Then he recited His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not considered what things Allah has created, how their shadows turn about...﴾ up to the end of the verse.

Al-Dahhak said: what is meant by the prostration of shadows is the prostration of the persons themselves.

Some of them mentioned that the meaning of His saying ﴿sujjadan li-llah﴾ is: submissive, humbled, serving in what they were intended for by their original creation. All things are naturally disposed to what they were intended for in their original creation.

Some of them mentioned that He attributed prostration to these things only because they call to prostration, so it is as if they themselves were prostrating. The more sound view is the first, then the second.

His saying: ﴿wa hum dakhirun﴾ (while they are humbled) means: abased.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 49:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures that move﴾. The meaning of "creatures that move" (dabba) here, they said, is the living beings, because it is the nature of living beings to crawl about. It is also said: "And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens, of the angels, and whatever is on the earth of creatures that move."

If someone says: how does this meaning hold, when after it He said: ﴿and the angels﴾?

The answer comes in two respects. The first: He singled them out for mention to honour them.

The second: the "angels" mentioned last are the angels of Allah on the earth, who worship Allah the Most High and glorify Him. His words ﴿and they are not arrogant﴾: istikbar (arrogance) means seeking greatness by abandoning submission to the truth.

The Exalted said: ﴿They fear their Lord above them﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is that they fear the punishment of their Lord that comes from above them. The second view, which is the more correct one, is that this is the attribute of highness (al-'uluw) which Allah has singled Himself out with, and it is as He described Himself, without specifying its modality (takyif, assigning it a particular how).

As for His saying: ﴿and they do what they are commanded﴾, it means that the angels do not disobey Him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 51:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And Allah said: Do not take two gods﴾. If someone asks: what is the meaning of His words ﴿two﴾ (ithnayn), when He has said ﴿gods﴾ (ilahayn)?

The answer has two aspects. The first is by way of emphasis, and it is like the words of the Exalted: {Then a fast of three days during the Hajj and seven when you have returned; those are ten complete} (Qur'an 2:196).

The second answer is that the verse is in the form of inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir), and its meaning is: "And Allah said: Do not take two gods, two; it is only one God. ﴿So fear Me alone﴾," meaning: fear Me.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 52:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, its meaning is well known. And His statement: ﴿And to Him is obedience (al-din) perpetual (wasiban)﴾, i.e., constant (da'iman), thus said Ibn 'Abbas, and al-din (religion, obedience) means obedience (ta'ah).

The reality of the meaning is that the obedience of other than God is cut off and passes away, while the obedience of God does not pass away and is not cut off. It was also said: "wasiban" means sincere (khalisan). In the language, al-wasab is fatigue (al-ta'ab), so it is said, according to this, that the meaning of the verse is that all acts of obedience belong to God, even if there is in them wasab and fatigue.

His statement: ﴿Do you then fear other than God?﴾, i.e., do you fear, and this is a question in the manner of denunciation (al-inkar).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 53:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from Allah﴾. Its meaning: "And whatever blessing you have (yakun lakum) is from Allah." In some of the musnads, through the narration of Ibn 'Umar from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "No servant is touched by a blessing and knows that it is from Allah without having thanked Allah, even if he does not praise Him."

And His saying: ﴿Then when harm touches you﴾. It was said: this refers to drought (al-qahṭ), and it was said: to illness (al-marḍ). And His saying: ﴿then to Him you cry for help﴾. Al-ju'ar is the sound made in the manner of seeking aid (al-istighathah), and from it comes the lowing of cattle (ju'ar al-baqar). The meaning of the verse is that you call upon Allah while seeking His help. The poet said:

(He passes between the prayers to the King... sometimes in prostration, and sometimes in ju'ar)

Almost there, but one note on the quotation markers: the verse text here is ﴿ثمَّ إِذا كشف الضّر عَنْكُم﴾ and ﴿إِذا فريق مِنْكُم برَبهمْ يشركُونَ﴾, which I will render with the ﴿ ﴾ markers as instructed.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then, when harm is removed from you﴾ means: the harm that afflicts you. And His saying: ﴿behold, a group of you associate others with their Lord﴾ means: they disbelieve.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 55:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That they may disbelieve in what We have given them﴾. Its meaning is that the outcome of their affair is their disbelief in the blessing We have bestowed upon them. This lam and its like are called the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah). It is also said: the blessing is the signs which He showed His creation as evidence of His oneness.

And His saying: ﴿So enjoy yourselves﴾, meaning: live out the period that has been set for you in the pursuit of pleasure. ﴿But you will come to know﴾ the consequence of your affair.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 56:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And they assign to what they do not know a share of what We have provided for them﴾. Its meaning: they assign to the idols a share of what We have provided for them. This is the meaning of the Most High's words: ﴿They say, "This is for God," by their claim, and "This is for our partners."﴾ And His words: ﴿what they do not know﴾ mean: they do not know that they (the idols) harm them and do not benefit them.

And His words: ﴿By God, you will certainly be questioned about what you used to fabricate﴾. Its meaning: "By God, you will certainly be questioned." The questioning here is questioning to establish the proof (ilzam al-hujjah), not questioning seeking information or inquiry.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 57:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And they attribute daughters to Allah﴾. This is the meaning of their saying that the angels are the daughters of Allah. And His words: ﴿Glory be to Him﴾ are an explanation of His exemption from their saying.

And His words: ﴿And for themselves is what they desire﴾, meaning: the sons, for they used to say that He has the daughters, while we have the sons.

And His saying: ﴿When one of them is given the good news of a female﴾ — the people of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) used to prefer males among their children and dislike females, and they would say: "Indeed, they do not fight, nor do they ride horses." A man among them, when his wife's time of delivery drew near, would hide himself from his people; if he was given the good news of a son, he would appear, and the people would congratulate him. But if he was given the good news of a female, he would change color and go into hiding, and sometimes he would bury her alive (wa'd). So this is the meaning.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 16, verse 59:

His saying: ﴿He hides himself from the people because of the evil of that which he has been given good news of﴾, meaning: because of his aversion to what he has been given good news of.

As for His saying: ﴿His face becomes dark, and he is filled with suppressed grief﴾, its meaning: his face changed from grief. The Arabs say: "The face of so-and-so turned black" when it changes due to the sorrow that has befallen him.

And His saying: ﴿and he is filled with suppressed grief﴾, that is, full of sorrow. Ibn 'Abbas said: "grieving." Others said: "He was filled with grief, so he suppresses it (yakzimuhu), that is, he holds it in and does not show it."

As for His saying: ﴿Will he keep it in spite of disgrace?﴾ al-Jahdari read: "ʿalā hawān" (in disgrace). al-Kisa'i said: "al-hawn and al-hawan have the same meaning." al-Khansa' said in verse:

(They humble the souls, and the weakening of the souls... for the day of battle it preserves them.)

'Isa ibn 'Umar read: "am yadussuhā fī al-turāb" (or bury it in the dust), and according to this reading it would necessarily be read "ayumsikuhā" (keep it). As for the well-known reading, it refers back to the word "mā" (that which), and "mā" means "alladhī" (that which).

His saying: ﴿or bury it in the dust﴾, that is, bury it alive. Qatada said: "How many a female is better for her family than a male." In some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ) it is said that he said: "No woman gives birth to a daughter except that the angel places his hand on her head and says: 'A weak one has come forth from a weak one; whoever cares for her will be aided until the Day of Resurrection.'"

His saying: ﴿Surely evil is what they judge﴾, that is, evil is what they judge, and their judgment is burying daughters alive and leaving sons.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 60:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the attribute of evil﴾. That is, the attribute of evil. It was also said: the outcome of evil. And His statement: ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest attribute﴾. That is, the highest description, such as the descriptions "Knowing," "Powerful," "Provider," "Living," and other than these.

Mujahid said: "And to Allah belongs the highest attribute" is the testimony that there is no god but Allah. If it is said: He has said in another place, ﴿So do not strike forth comparisons for Allah﴾, and here He has said ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest attribute﴾. How is the reconciliation between them? The answer is that the meaning of His statement ﴿So do not strike forth comparisons for Allah﴾ is: the comparisons which are likenesses, for Allah, exalted is He, has no likeness. As for His statement ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest attribute﴾, it means the highest description, and this is permissible for everyone to say, indeed obligatory. And His statement ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾ has already been explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 61:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And if Allah were to seize mankind for their wrongdoing﴾, that is, for their disbelief. And His words: ﴿He would not leave upon it any creature﴾. It is related from ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud that he said: "Indeed the dung beetle in its hole is punished for the sins of the children of Adam." And it is related from Abu Hurayrah that he heard a man say: "Indeed the wrongdoer harms only himself," so he said to him: "How evil is what you have said! Indeed the bustard dies of emaciation because of the wrongdoing of the wrongdoer."

And some of the scholars of the meanings (ahl al-maʿani) said that the meaning of the verse is: if He were to seize the wrongdoers and destroy the fathers, the offspring would cease, and the children would not exist, so that whoever is on the earth would be destroyed.

And His words: ﴿But He gives them respite until a specified term﴾, meaning: until the Day of Resurrection. And His words: ﴿So when their term comes, they will not delay it by an hour, nor will they hasten it﴾ — the meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 62:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they attribute to Allah what they dislike﴾ means: the daughters. And His saying: ﴿And their tongues describe the lie﴾ — the lie mentioned is their saying: ﴿that for them is the best﴾.

Regarding "the best" (al-husna) there are two opinions: one, that it is sons; the other, that it is Paradise. And His saying: ﴿Undoubtedly, for them is the Fire﴾ — "la" (no) is a rejection of their claim. And His saying: ﴿jaram﴾ means "truly." It has also been said: "Undoubtedly for them is the Fire"; and it has been said: "there is no doubt" (la budd). We have already explained that jarama means "to earn" (kasaba), and we cited poetic evidence for it.

And His saying: ﴿and that they are mufrat-un (neglected/sent forward)﴾ — most of the reciters read it with a fathah on the ra'. Nafi' read "mufrit-un" with a kasrah, and Abu Ja'far al-Madani read "mufarrit-un" with a shaddah on the ra'.

Opinions differ regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿mufrat-un﴾ with a fathah on the ra'. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: "forgotten (mansiyyun)." It is also reported from them: "abandoned (matrukun)." It has been said: "lost/neglected (mudayya'un)." And from al-Hasan al-Basri: "sent ahead to the Fire (muqaddamun ila al-nar)." From this comes the word al-fārit (forerunner), which is the one who goes ahead to the water. The poet said:

(They hurried us, and they were among our companions, as a forerunner goes ahead of the one coming to water)

And it is firmly established from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "I am your fārat (forerunner) at the Basin," meaning: one who precedes you. Al-Kisa'i, Abu 'Ubayda and al-Farra' preferred the meaning given by Mujahid.

As for His saying "mufrit-un" with a kasrah on the ra', it is from al-ifrat (excess), meaning: those who exceed in wrongdoing. And as for "mufarrit-un," it is from al-tafrit (negligence), meaning: those who fall short.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 63:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿By Allah, We certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you﴾, meaning: By Allah, We certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you. And His saying: ﴿So Satan made their deeds appear fair to them﴾, meaning: their disbelief and denial. And His saying: ﴿So he is their ally today﴾, He called him their ally because of their obedience to him. And His saying: ﴿And they will have a painful punishment﴾, meaning: painful (mu'lim).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 64:

His saying: ﴿And We have not sent down to you the Book except that you may make clear to them that about which they differ﴾. The difference between tabyin (making clear, elucidation) and tamyiz (distinguishing) is that tabyin involves seeking knowledge, whereas tamyiz does not involve seeking knowledge, for a man distinguishes between the good and the bad [while] (already) knowing them both.

And His saying: ﴿about which they differ﴾, that is: concerning the Book. And His saying: ﴿and as a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe﴾, its meaning is that the Book is a guidance and a mercy for the believers. It has also been said: the Messenger is a guidance and a mercy for the believers.

God Most High says: ﴿And Allah sends down water from the sky﴾, meaning: the rain. And His saying: ﴿and with it He gives life to the earth after its death﴾, meaning: with vegetation. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for a people who listen﴾, meaning: who listen with understanding.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 66:

The Most High's saying: ﴿And indeed, in the livestock there is a lesson for you. We give you to drink from what is in their bellies﴾. It has been recited with the accusative (nasb) and with the nominative (raf'). As for the accusative, its meaning is well known. As for the nominative, it means that [the livestock] makes for you a drink (suqya). The poet said, distinguishing between the two:

(Let my people, the Banu Majd, be given drink, and let me give drink to Numayr and the tribes of Hilal)

His saying: ﴿from what is in their bellies﴾. If it is asked: why did He not say "from what is in their bellies" (feminine, butunuha), since al-An'am is a collective noun? The answer: its meaning is "from what is in the bellies of each of the two kinds, or each type among them." The Arabs do omit such things. The poet said:

(O Suhayl, al-Qutaykh has spoiled, and the milk of the camels has become pleasant and cool) meaning: it has become cool.

His saying: ﴿from between excrement and blood﴾. The fars (excrement) is what collects in the rumen of weight. It is said that the fodder which the animal eats changes in the rumen and turns into milk, excrement and blood. Its upper part is blood, its middle is milk, and its lower part is excrement. Then God Most High distinguishes between them, so each one flows in its own course separately. He places the milk in the udder, He places the blood in the veins, and the excrement remains in the rumen. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿from between excrement and blood﴾.

His saying: ﴿pure milk﴾, meaning: it has neither the color of blood nor the smell of excrement. His saying: ﴿palatable (sa'if)﴾. The sa'if is that which goes down the throat easily. In some reports: no one has choked on milk, based on His saying: ﴿palatable﴾. His saying: ﴿for those who drink﴾, its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 67:

His saying: ﴿And from the fruits of the date palms and the grapes you take from them intoxicant (sakar) and good provision﴾. The scholars differed concerning the sakar. What is related from Ibn 'Abbas is that the sakar is what is forbidden from the fruit, and the good provision is what is lawful from the fruit. And from Mujahid, Qatadah, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and al-Sha'bi: that the verse is abrogated (mansukh, i.e. its ruling has been replaced by a later one), and this was before the prohibition of wine, after which it was prohibited.

It is related from al-Sha'bi that he said: the sakar is nabidh (fermented drink), and the good provision is dates and raisins. This is the view of those who permit nabidh. As for the view of Ibn 'Abbas, the meaning of the verse is a report about them, not a permission for them. The most preferred of the opinions is that His saying ﴿you take from it intoxicant﴾ is abrogated.

In some of the musnad collections it is related that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "For you from grapes there are five lawful things: the juice (al-'asir), the raisins (al-zabib), the vinegar (al-khall), the rub (al-rubb), and that you eat it as grapes." And God knows best its authenticity. The poet said concerning the sakar:

(Evil is their bedfellow and evil is their drink, when the mizza and the sakar flow among them)

That is: the intoxicant (al-muskir). As for His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reason﴾, its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 68:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And your Lord inspired the bee﴾ to the end of the verse. "And your Lord inspired" means: your Lord caused to instinct (alhama). Linguistically, wahy (revelation, inspiration) is the informing of a thing in concealment, and it may be by writing, may be by gesture, may be by inspiration (ilham), and may be by hidden speech. Some of them said the meaning of His saying: ﴿And your Lord inspired the bee﴾ is: He placed this in their natures (gharaʾiz). It was also said: awhā (inspired) here means sakhkhara (subjected) and dhallala (made submissive). The most sound of the sayings is the first. As for His saying: ﴿to the bee﴾, al-nahl (the bee) is the fly of honey (dhubab al-ʿasal). In a report from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "Every fly is in the Fire except the bee." But the report is gharib (rare, of weak chain).

As for His saying: ﴿that take for yourselves dwellings in the mountains and in the trees﴾, that is, khalaya (hives), which are the places where the bee deposits honey. It is said that it only deposits honey in the hollows of trees, and it may deposit it on the branches of trees. As for His saying: ﴿and in what they construct﴾, it means: what they build. It has been the custom of its people that they build places for it, so it takes refuge in them by God's subjecting it to that.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 69:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then eat from all the fruits and follow the ways of your Lord.﴾ That is, the paths of your Lord. Mujahid said: "They follow their paths, and no place is rugged for them."

﴿There emerges from their bellies a drink of varying colors, in which is healing for mankind. Indeed, in that is a sign for a people who give thought.﴾

As for His saying: ﴿Subservient (dhululan)﴾, it may have two meanings:

It may refer to the paths: one says "a sabil dhalul" and "subul dhulul" when the way is easy to traverse. It may also refer to the bees, meaning that they are obedient and submissive to that for which they were created. It is said that the bees have a yu'sub (leader of the bees), which is their chief: when he halts, they halt, and when he moves, they move. It is also said that "dhululan" means submissive to their keepers, for it has been the custom that their keepers move them from place to place, so they are made subservient for that purpose.

As for His saying: ﴿There emerges from their bellies﴾. If someone says: Does it not emerge from their mouths rather than their bellies? The answer is that He mentioned their bellies because the transformation takes place in their bellies, and because it comes out of their bellies toward their mouths, and then it flows from their mouths like saliva. It is narrated that Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) passed by Abd al-Rahman ibn Attab ibn Usayd, who had been killed on the Day of the Camel, and said: "This is the yu'sub of Quraysh. I have been cured, and my people have been killed. I complain to Allah of my ajari and bajari," meaning my worries and my sorrows.

As for His saying: ﴿a drink of varying colors﴾, it means red, yellow, and white. As for His saying: ﴿in which is healing for mankind﴾, there is no doubt for anyone that there is healing in honey for some diseases, and it is included in electuaries and many medicines. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: "In it is healing for mankind" means in the Qur'an. The more apparent view regarding the verse is the first opinion.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated that a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned that his brother was suffering from a stomach ailment. He said: "Give him honey to drink." He gave him to drink, and the pain increased. He returned and mentioned this, and he said: "Give him honey to drink." He gave him to drink and his pain increased. He returned, and this happened repeatedly. He said: "Give him honey to drink," and he gave him to drink, and he was cured. He returned and mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Allah has spoken the truth, and your brother's stomach has lied."

It is also reported from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "Whoever suffers from any ailment should take four dirhams from his wife's dower, buy honey with them, mix it with rainwater, and drink it, for in it is healing."

When Ibn Umar was afflicted with pain, he would apply honey to the place of pain, even to a boil. It is reported from Abu Harra that he used to apply honey to his eyes as kohl. As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for a people who give thought﴾, that is, who reflect.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 70:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah created you, then He takes you back [in death]; and among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age﴾. He means: senility (al-haram). It is reported from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: it is seventy-five years. It is also said: eighty years, related by Qutrub. It is also said: ninety years. It is reported from ʿIkrimah that he said: whoever recites the Qur'an will not be returned to the most decrepit age. Its meaning is that his intellect will not depart and he will not become senile (yakhrif). It is also said: the return to the most decrepit age is for the disbelievers, for Allah exalted says: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe﴾.

And His saying: ﴿so that he knows nothing after having known﴾. He means: his knowledge and intellect will diminish. This is evidence that a thing may be mentioned while what is meant is the majority of it, for when one is returned to the most decrepit age, all of his knowledge does not depart; rather, most of his knowledge departs. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Powerful﴾ is clear in meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 71:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah has favoured some of you over others in provision﴾. Its meaning: He extends it for this one and restricts it for that one, and gives more to this one and less to that one.

And His saying: ﴿So those who have been favoured will not hand over their provision to those whom their right hands possess, so that they would be equal in it﴾. In the verse there is a refutation of the polytheists in their taking idols as gods alongside Allah. The meaning of the verse is: the free owners among you do not willingly give up their wealth to their slaves so that the slaves might share with them in ownership, becoming equal to them. If you do not accept this for yourselves, then it is more fitting that you exalt your Lord above it. A parallel to this is what is mentioned in Surat al-Rum: ﴿He presents to you a parable from yourselves…﴾ up to His saying: ﴿so that you are equal therein﴾.

And His saying: ﴿Then do they deny the favour of Allah?﴾ meaning: they deny that He has bestowed favours upon them, and they take others besides Him as gods alongside Him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 72:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah has made for you spouses from among yourselves﴾. On this there are two opinions. The first: this refers to Adam, peace be upon him, for Allah, exalted is He, created Hawwa' (Eve) from part of his ribs.

The second opinion: "He created for you spouses from among yourselves" means spouses of your own kind, i.e. from your own species.

And His saying: ﴿and made for you, from your spouses, sons and grandchildren (ḥafadah)﴾. Regarding al-ḥafadah there are several opinions. It is narrated from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that he said: they are the in-laws by marriage of two sisters (al-akhtān). And also from him that he said: they are the relatives by marriage (al-aṣhār). The meaning of the verse according to this opinion is: "And He made for you, from your spouses, sons and daughters whom you marry off, so that through them you gain in-laws by marriage (akhtān and aṣhār)."

And from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, Mujahid, and others, that they said: they are the servants (khadam). And from al-Hasan al-Basri he said: they are the helpers (a'wan). It was also said: the children's children (awlād al-awlād). And it was said: the children of a woman by her other husband.

Al-ḥafd in the language means hastening in work. In the supplication of qunut: "And to You we strive and hasten (naḥfid)," i.e. we hasten. And the poet said:

(The female servants hastened around them, and they surrendered to their hands the reins of the camels.)

It was also said: the sons (banīn) are the adults, and the ḥafadah are the young children. It is said that there is inversion (taqdīm wa ta'khīr) in the verse, and its meaning is: "And He made for you helpers, and from your spouses sons."

His saying: ﴿and provided you with good things﴾, meaning: lawful blessings.

His saying: ﴿Then in falsehood do they believe?﴾ This is in the manner of denunciation. His saying: {and in the favor of Allah do they disbelieve?} meaning: in Islam they disbelieve. It was also said: in their Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) they disbelieve.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that which possesses for them no provision from the heavens or the earth in the least, and they are not able [to do anything]﴾. The purpose of the verse is to mention the incapacity of the idols to bring about any benefit or to ward off any harm.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 74:

And His saying: ﴿So do not strike forth comparisons for God﴾, meaning: al-amthal (the likenesses, the similitudes). Its meaning is: do not make for God any likeness (shabah) or any equal (mithl), for there is no likeness to Him and no equal to Him. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, God knows, while you do not know﴾ is apparent in meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 75:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿God strikes a parable: a slave owned, who has no power over anything, and one whom We have provided with good provision from Us, so that he spends from it secretly and openly. Are they equal? Praise belongs to God. But most of them do not know.﴾ Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: the parable was struck for Himself and for the idol that was worshipped besides Him. So His saying, ﴿a slave owned﴾, He meant by it the idol. And His saying, ﴿and one whom We have provided with good provision from Us﴾, is a parable struck for Himself, in the sense that He is the Generous Provider who gives from where the servant knows and from where the servant does not know.

Qatada said – and this is the second opinion – that it is a parable for the disbeliever and the believer. So His saying, ﴿a slave owned﴾, He meant by it the disbeliever, and His saying, ﴿and one whom We have provided with good provision﴾, He meant by it the believer. It was said: the first opinion is more fitting to the apparent meaning of the verse, because mention of the idols came first, and (the mention of the idols came later).

As for those who upheld the second opinion, they argued for its soundness with His saying, ﴿a slave owned﴾, and an idol is not called a slave. In some narrations from Ibn Abbas, the verse concerns two specific men: as for the one whom God provided with good provision, so that he spends from it secretly and openly, he is ʿAmr ibn Hisham; and as for the owned slave, he is his master Abu al-Jawab, who used to order him to believe and he refused. Al-Nahhas (Abu Jaʿfar al-Nahhas) cited it in his tafsir with its chain of transmission.

As for His saying, ﴿Are they equal?﴾: if someone says: how did He say "Are they equal?" when the parable was struck for two persons? The answer: what is meant is the category, not one particular individual. As for His saying, ﴿Praise belongs to God, but most of them do not know﴾, its meaning is apparent: He praises Himself for His knowledge and their ignorance. It was also said: its meaning is: say, "Praise belongs to God" for what the evidence has made clear and what has been manifested of the truth, but most of them do not know. And it is said: "Praise belongs to me, for I am the one deserving of praise, not what they associate with Me, but most of them do not know that I am the one deserving of praise."

"The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And Allah presents a parable: two men, one of whom is mute﴾. Al-abkam (the mute) is the one who cannot speak, does not understand, and does not comprehend. And His words: ﴿who has no power over anything﴾ mean: he has no power to speak.

And His words: ﴿and he is a burden upon his master﴾ mean: he is a burden upon his master. And His words: ﴿wherever he directs him, he brings no good﴾ mean: wherever he sends him, he is not guided to any good. And His words: ﴿Are they equal, he and one who enjoins justice﴾ refer by this to himself, whereas Allah the Exalted enjoins justice and acts with justice.

And His words: ﴿while he is on a straight path﴾ mean: on an upright way. The meaning of the verse is: He struck another parable for Himself and for the idols. The first is the idol, and what is meant by ﴿and one who enjoins justice﴾ is Allah the Exalted. And His words: ﴿on a straight path﴾ are because Allah the Exalted is on the path of truth, and there is no deviation from Him.

There is another opinion regarding the verse, which is what is related from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: The verse concerns two specific men. As for the first, he is Usayd ibn Abi al-'Ays. And His words: ﴿and one who enjoins justice﴾ is 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, and 'Uthman used to call him to Islam, but he would not embrace it."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 77:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾ means: the knowledge of the unseen of the heavens and the earth. And His saying: ﴿And the matter of the Hour is but as the blink of an eye﴾ means: when He says to it, "Be," it is.

And His saying: ﴿Or it is closer﴾ means: nearer than the blink of an eye. If it is said: how does He say ﴿or it is closer﴾, when "or" (aw) indicates doubt, and that is not permissible for Allah?

The answer is in two respects. The first: His saying ﴿or it is closer﴾ means "rather, it is closer," as the poet said:

(It appeared like the disc of the sun in the brightness of the forenoon... and its radiance, or you are more graceful in the eye.)

That is: rather, you are more graceful in the eye.

The second answer: what is meant is "or it is closer in your knowledge." And His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾ is clear in meaning.

The Exalted said: ﴿And Allah brought you out from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing﴾. He means: you did not know anything of what you know now.

And His saying: ﴿And He made for you hearing and sight and hearts﴾. That is, the faculties of hearing, sight, and hearts (al-af'idah), and al-fu'ad is the singular of af'idah. And His saying: ﴿so that you may be grateful﴾. That is, grateful for My blessing upon you.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 79:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have they not seen the birds subjected in the midst of the sky?﴾ That is: made subservient in the middle of the heavens. It is related from Ka'b al-Ahbar (a Companion-era scholar of Jewish origin, known for transmitting Isra'iliyyat) that the bird rises twelve miles and does not rise above this. Above the atmosphere (al-jaww) is al-sakkak, and above al-sakkak is the heaven.

And His saying: ﴿None holds them up except Allah﴾ means: while they are flying, and in their gathering and spreading of their wings.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ means: lessons.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 80:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And God has made for you, from your houses, a place of rest﴾, i.e., places in which you dwell. And His saying: ﴿and He has made for you, from the hides of the cattle, tents﴾, meaning: the pavilions, the tents and the domes made of leather (adam).

And His saying: ﴿that you find light to carry﴾, meaning: their carrying is made easy for you. And His saying: ﴿on the day of your traveling﴾, meaning: the day of your journey. And His saying: ﴿and on the day of your settling﴾, i.e., at the time of your residing.

And His saying: ﴿and from their wool, their fur, and their hair, furnishings and provision for a time﴾. "Aṣwāf" (wool) is for sheep, "awbār" (fur) is for camels, and "ash'ār" (hair) is for goats. And His saying: ﴿athāth﴾ (furnishings). Al-athāth (furnishings) is the household goods, that is, what one furnishes oneself with (yatha'aththathu bihi), i.e., benefits from. The poet said:

(Did the litters of the women, on the day they departed, stir your longing, with their fine adornments of furnishings?)

It is also said: al-athāth is clothing. And His saying: ﴿and provision for a time﴾, i.e., enjoyment until the time of your appointed terms.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 81:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah has made for you, from what He has created, shades﴾, meaning: that which shades you from the sun, such as trees, walls, roofs, mountains, and the like.

And His saying: ﴿and He has made for you, from the mountains, shelters﴾, meaning: caves and clefts. Al-akinan (shelters) is the plural of al-kinn (shelter). And His saying: ﴿and He has made for you garments﴾, meaning: shirts. They may be of wool, they may be of cotton, and they may be of linen.

And His saying: ﴿that protect you from the heat﴾. Here there is an ellipsis, and its meaning is: that protect you from the heat and the cold. The poet said:

(And I do not know, when I set out for a land, desiring good, which of the two will befall me.)

Al-Nahhas said: "He desires good and guards against evil, since everyone who desires good guards against evil. And his saying, 'which of the two will befall me,' means: the good or the evil."

And His saying: ﴿and garments that protect you from your violence﴾, meaning: coats of mail. Al-ba's (violence) is that by which violence occurs, namely weapons.
