And His saying: ﴿Thus does He complete His favour upon you﴾, meaning: His bounty upon you. And His saying: ﴿that you may submit (to Him)﴾, meaning: that you may believe. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he recited, "la'allakum tuslamun" (that you may be safe), and this reading is uncommon.

If it is asked: Why did He mention these blessings, the mountains, shades, garments, shirts, fur and wool, when Allah, may He be exalted, has many blessings beyond these that He did not mention? What is the purpose of singling out these blessings and leaving aside what is greater than them?

The answer to this is: the Arabs were people of livestock, they were people of mountains, and their lands were hot. So He mentioned the blessings that suit their circumstances, and these blessings were, for them, above every blessing. Therefore He singled them out for mention for this reason. And it is related from Qatadah that this surah is called the Surah of Blessings.

Almighty God says: ﴿But if they turn away, then upon you is only the clear conveyance﴾. This is consolation for the Prophet. Its meaning: if they turn away, no blame or mark of failure shall fall upon you for that; upon you is only the conveyance, and you have conveyed.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 83:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They recognise the blessing of Allah, then they deny it﴾. Al-Suddi said: "It is Muhammad (ﷺ)." Many of the people of tafsir (exegesis) hold this view. It is also said that its meaning is Islam.

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that the meaning of the verse is: when they were asked, "Who gave you these blessings?", they would say, "Allah." But when they were told, "Then affirm His oneness," they would say, "We were given them through the intercession of our gods."

And from Qatadah: they acknowledge that the blessings come from Allah, then when they are told, "Give charity, and comply with what Allah has commanded in them," they say, "We inherited them from our fathers."

And from 'Awn ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: denying a blessing is that a person says, "Had it not been for such-and-such, I would have been afflicted with such-and-such, and had it not been for so-and-so, it would have befallen me."

And from al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: the blessings are six: Muhammad (ﷺ), the Qur'an, Islam, well-being, concealment (of faults), and independence from people.

His saying: ﴿and most of them are disbelievers﴾, meaning: all of them are disbelievers, because the verse concerns the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 84:

The Exalted One's saying: ﴿And on the Day We raise up from every nation a witness﴾ has the same meaning as His saying: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and bring you as a witness against these people?﴾

And His saying: "Then those who disbelieved will not be permitted," meaning: to make excuses. It is said: [it means] to speak at all. And His saying: ﴿nor will they be asked to make amends﴾ means: they will not be returned to the world so that they may repent. The real meaning of al-isti'tab (seeking to make amends) is: an approach aimed at seeking pleasure [of the one wronged], and this avenue is closed to the disbelievers in the Hereafter.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when those who did wrong see the punishment﴾. He means: Hell (jahannam). And His saying: ﴿it will not be lightened for them﴾ means: it will not be made easier for them. And His saying: ﴿nor will they be reprieved﴾ means: they will not be given respite.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 86:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿When those who associated partners with Allah see their partners﴾. This is at the time when Allah raises the idols and brings them forth. When the disbelievers see them, ﴿they will say: "Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to invoke besides You."﴾

As for His words: ﴿But they will throw back at them the word: "Indeed, you are liars."﴾ there are two opinions regarding it:

The more apparent view is that this is the speech of the idols, who say to the polytheists: "Indeed, you are liars," meaning: in claiming that we invited you to worship us, or in your saying that these are gods, or in your saying that we deserve to be worshipped.

The second opinion is that it is the angels who say: "Indeed, you are liars."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 87:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they will offer submission to Allah that Day﴾, meaning: the worshipper and the worshipped will submit to Allah, may He be exalted. His saying: ﴿and what they used to invent will vanish from them﴾, meaning: what they used to lie about will perish for them. The real meaning is that what they claimed has been lost to them, for it was a fabrication and a lie.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 88:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who disbelieve and bar from the way of Allah﴾, meaning: they prevented people from the path of truth. And His saying: ﴿We will increase them in punishment upon punishment﴾. Masruq narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud that he said: "Scorpions like mules." In another narration from him: "Serpents like elephants, and scorpions like tall palm trees." And from Abu al-Zahiriyya who said: "There is no punishment that people know, or that they do not know, except that Allah punishes the people of the Fire with it." It is also related that they flee from the Fire, and so they come out to a zamharir (bitter cold) in Hell, which is more severe upon them than the Fire; so they return to the Fire, seeking refuge in it. And His saying: ﴿Because of what they used to corrupt﴾, i.e.: [they used to associate partners with Allah].

And the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And on the Day We raise up in every nation a witness against them from among themselves, and We bring you as a witness against these people﴾. We have already explained its meaning.

And His saying: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an exposition of all things﴾, that is: an exposition of the reward and the punishment, and of the lawful (ḥalāl) and the unlawful (ḥarām). It is related from al-Awzā'ī that he said: "An exposition by means of the Sunnah."

And His saying: ﴿and guidance﴾, that is: from misguidance. And His saying: ﴿and mercy﴾, that is: a kindness toward those to whom it was sent down. And His saying: ﴿and good tidings﴾, that is: glad tidings ﴿for the Muslims﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 90:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah orders justice and grace﴾ There are several opinions regarding this verse. The first: that justice (al-'adl) is the testimony that there is no god but Allah. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas and others. It has also been said that it is tawhid (affirmation of Allah's oneness), which has the same meaning as the first.

﴿Allah orders justice and grace and giving to relatives, and forbids immorality, wrongdoing and oppression﴾

The second opinion: that it is fairness (al-insaf) and abandoning injustice (al-jawr). It is related from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi that Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz summoned him when he assumed the caliphate and said to him: "Describe justice to me." He replied: "Be a father to the young, a son to the old, a brother to your peers, punish people in proportion to their sins, and beware of striking anyone out of your anger." The third opinion: that justice is that a person's inner state and outward appearance are equal.

As for the words of Allah, ﴿and grace﴾, it means that a person's inner state be better than his outward appearance in the sight of Allah. Regarding His words ﴿and grace﴾ there are several opinions: The first: that grace is pardon. The second: that it is performing the obligatory duties. The third: that you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you. The fourth: that it is going beyond what is required (al-tafaddul). It has also been said: grace is that a person's inner state be better than his outward appearance.

As for His words ﴿and giving to relatives﴾, it means maintaining the ties of kinship. It has also been said that this includes all of the children of Adam, because there is a bond between him and all of them through Adam, peace be upon him. The least of what falls under maintaining ties is refraining from harming, and wishing for him what one wishes for oneself, and disliking for him what one dislikes for oneself.

As for His words ﴿and forbids immorality﴾, al-fahsha' (immorality) is everything among sins that is considered abhorrent. It has also been said that it is fornication, and it has been said that it is miserliness, and it has been said that al-fahsha' is that a person's outward appearance be more shameful than his inner state.

As for His words ﴿and wrongdoing﴾, it means everything that is reprehensible in religion. It has been said that it is shirk, for it is the greatest of reprehensible things.

As for His words ﴿and oppression﴾, it is said that it is injustice and domineering over people. It has been said that it is arrogance, and it has been said that it is backbiting. Qatadah said: Allah the Exalted gathered in this verse everything He loves and everything He dislikes.

It is mentioned in some of the musnads that Shutayr came to Masruq and said to him: "Either you narrate to me from 'Abdullah and I will affirm you, or I narrate to you from 'Abdullah and you affirm me." He said: "You narrate." So he said: "I heard 'Abdullah say: The most comprehensive verse in the Qur'an for good and evil is the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah orders justice and grace﴾." Masruq said to him: "You have spoken the truth."

It is said: justice is the zakat of authority, pardon is the zakat of power, grace is the zakat of blessing, and writing to brothers is the zakat of standing; i.e., the writing of intercession.

As for the words of Allah the Exalted, ﴿He admonishes you, so that you may remember﴾, it means: that you may take heed.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 91:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And fulfil the covenant of God when you have made a covenant﴾, to the end of the verse. He said: The covenant here is the oath (yamin). It is related from Jabir ibn Zayd and al-Sha'bi that both of them said: The covenant is an oath, and its expiation is the expiation of an oath.

It is related from Umar that he said: The promise is part of the covenant. The same is related from Ibn Abbas.

As for His statement: ﴿And do not break your oaths after their confirmation﴾, that is, after their solemnising (ihkam), ﴿and you have made God your surety over you﴾, that is, a witness (shahid). It was also said: you have bound yourselves by His name, as one is bound by a surety (kafil). As for His statement: ﴿Indeed, God knows what you do﴾, it is a warning and a threat.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 92:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And be not like her who unravels her yarn﴾. This was a woman called Rayta bint Sa'd, who had a compulsive disorder (waswasa). She would sit beside a rock and spin all day long with a large spindle, and when evening came she would unravel it.

It is also said: she used to order her slave-girls to unravel it. Thus God likened those who break the covenant to her. Its meaning is that she did not cease from work, and when she had worked she did not cease from unravelling; likewise, you neither ceased from the covenant, nor when you made the covenant did you fulfil it.

His saying: ﴿after it has been made firm﴾, that is, after it has been strengthened. His saying: ﴿into shreds﴾, that is, unravelled and cut apart.

His saying: ﴿making your oaths a means of deceit between you﴾, that is, deception and trickery.

Al-dakhl (deceit) is that which is inserted into a thing for corruption. It is said that al-daghl (treachery) is to show fidelity while concealing the breaking of it, and likewise al-dakhl.

His saying: ﴿lest one community should be more numerous than another community﴾, that is, more numerous. As for its meaning: it is narrated from Mujahid that he said: they used to make covenants with one people, and when they saw peoples who were mightier and more numerous than them, they broke the covenant of the former and made a covenant with the latter. Accordingly, His saying ﴿lest one community should be more numerous than another community﴾ means: you sought glory by breaking the covenant, because one community was more numerous than another.

There is another opinion regarding the verse: it was revealed concerning a people who made a covenant with the Prophet (ﷺ), then broke the covenant with him and made a covenant with a people of the disbelievers, thinking that their strength was greater because their number was greater. It is also said that the verse was revealed concerning the believers, and God forbade them from breaking the covenant; as if the Almighty said: when you make a covenant with a people out of fear, then when you are secure, do not break it, so that your side may be stronger and more numerous.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, God is only testing you thereby﴾, that is, by the multitude and the scarcity. It is also said: ﴿God is only testing you thereby﴾, that is, by the command to fulfil the covenant. His saying: ﴿And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 93:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one nation﴾, meaning: upon one religion, which is Islam. And His saying: ﴿But He sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾, and the verse is explicit in refuting the Qadariyya.

And His saying: ﴿But you will surely be questioned about what you used to do﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection. The real meaning is that I am not questioned about what I do of misguidance and guidance, while you are questioned about what you do of good and evil.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on Surah 16, verse 94:

Regarding His, the Exalted, words: ﴿And do not take your oaths as means of deception among you﴾, meaning: a cause of corruption among you. We have already explained the meaning of al-dakhl (deception, corruption, hidden defect).

Regarding His words: ﴿lest a foot slip after it was firmly planted﴾, meaning: slip away from Islam after it had been firmly established upon Islam. He said:

(Grammar is difficult and long, its safety lies in one who climbs it without knowing it...)

(His foot slipped with it down to the lowest depths...)

Regarding His words: ﴿and taste the evil﴾, meaning: the punishment. Regarding His words: ﴿because you turned people away from the way of Allah﴾, meaning: you made easy the path of breaking the covenant for people by your breaking the covenant. Regarding His words: ﴿and for you there will be a great punishment﴾, meaning: a mighty one.

"And do not sell the covenant of God for a small price." That is, for something trivial of the goods of this world. As for His words, "What is with God is better for you, if you only knew" — its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 16, verse 96:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿What you have will run out﴾ means that the world and whatever is in it will perish. His saying: ﴿But what is with Allah is everlasting﴾ means the Hereafter. The intelligent person should prefer what endures. In some reports it is said: "For this world there are sons, and for the Hereafter there are sons, so be among the sons of the Hereafter, and do not be among the sons of this world."

His saying: ﴿And We will surely reward those who were patient with their reward﴾ means: they were patient regarding the world. His saying: ﴿their reward﴾ means their recompense and their payment. His saying: ﴿according to the best of what they used to do﴾ means: according to the best of what they used to do.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 97:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾. The scholars differed concerning "a good life" (al-hayat al-tayyiba), in several opinions. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "The good life is lawful provision (al-rizq al-halal)." And from Mujahid and 'Ikrimah: that it is contentment (al-qana'a). In some of the supplications of the Prophet (ﷺ) he said: "O Allah, make me content with what You have provided me." And in the proverbial sayings: "Contentment is a hidden kingdom."

The third opinion: It is narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: "The good life is in Paradise." Al-Hasan said: "There is no good life in this world." And it is also narrated from him that he said: "The whole world is affliction; whatever good is in it is (only) a breeze." It is reported that he heard a man say to another: "May Allah never show you something disliked," so he said to him: "You have prayed to Allah for him to die, for this world is never free of what is disliked."

And from Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: "The good life is provision day by day." It was also said: it is the sweetness of worship and eating what is lawful. It is said: it is a person's living in his own land with sufficiency and well-being. And it was said: it is simply sufficiency and well-being.

As for His words: ﴿And We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾, the meaning has already been explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 98:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an﴾. It is related from Abu Hurayrah that he said: "Seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan after the recitation, because Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah﴾." Some have also related something similar from Malik.

The more correct view is that seeking refuge (isti'adhah) is before the recitation. This has been related through many reports from the Prophet (ﷺ). It has also been related from the Prophet (ﷺ), through the narration of Abu al-Mutawakkil al-Naji from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "When you begin the recitation, say: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan." And it is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from Shaytan, from his whisperings (hamz) and his blowing (nafth)."

As for the meaning of the verse: "When you intend to recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan." This is like the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer, wash﴾, meaning: when you intend to rise to prayer. In some reports it is said: there is nothing more severe upon Iblis than seeking refuge (isti'adhah). Seeking refuge in Allah is taking shelter in Allah (i'tisam billah).

As for His words: ﴿from the accursed Shaytan﴾, meaning: the stoned Shaytan (al-shaytan al-marjum).

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe﴾, meaning: he has no guardianship (wilayah) over those who believe. As for His saying: ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾, it is said that its meaning is: he is not able to cause them to fall into a sin for which they have no repentance. It is also said: he is not able to bring them into shirk (association of others with Allah) and to lead them astray.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 100:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, his authority is only over those who take him as an ally﴾, means: those who enter under his guardianship and follow him.

And His saying: ﴿and those who associate others with Him through him﴾. Some of them said: "they are associators with the Lord of the worlds." Thaʿlab said: "﴿and those who associate others with Him through him﴾, that is: for his sake they are associators, that is: for the sake of Iblis." This is a sound meaning, because whoever associates (partners) with Iblis is a believer in Allah, so the meaning is this.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 101:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when We substitute a verse in place of another verse﴾. The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: When a verse of severity (shiddah) was sent down to the Prophet and then abrogated (nuskhat), and a verse of leniency (lin) was sent down to him in its place, the polytheists said: "Look at this man, who changes the words of God on his own accord." They were saying, by way of mockery: "He replaces one thing with another." So God Exalted sent down this verse: ﴿And when We substitute a verse in place of another verse﴾, meaning: We put a verse in place of another verse.

His saying: ﴿And God knows best what He sends down﴾, meaning: God knows best what benefits His servants in what He sends down.

His saying: ﴿They say, "You are only a fabricator."﴾, meaning: a forger (mukhtalaq). His saying: ﴿But most of them do not know﴾, meaning: all of them do not know that I am the One who sends down all the verses, the abrogating (nasikh) and the abrogated (mansukh).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 102:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth﴾. That is, Jibril (Gabriel). And His saying: ﴿from your Lord in truth﴾, that is, with truthfulness. And His saying: ﴿to strengthen those who believe﴾, that is, to strengthen the hearts of those who believe.

And His saying: ﴿as a guidance and good tidings for the Muslims﴾. We have already explained the meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 103:

His saying: ﴿And We certainly know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches him."﴾ The verse… Opinions differed regarding the meaning of His saying: ﴿a human being﴾ (basharun). It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "He was a slave of ʿAmir ibn al-Hadrami, and he used to read the scriptures (al-kutub), and the polytheists claimed that the Messenger of Allah was learning from him." Mujahid said: "He was a slave of Huwaytib." Others said: "His name was Jabr." Some of them said: "Two slaves from ʿAyn al-Tamr, one of whom was called Jabr and the other Yasar, and they used to read the scriptures in their own language." Some of them said: "His name was Abu Fukayhah," and it was also said: "His name was ʿAyish." They said: "The Prophet used to sit with them and invite them to Islam, so Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse."

As for His saying: ﴿the tongue of him to whom they incline﴾ (lisan alladhi yulhidun ilayhi), it was recited as "yulhidun ilayhi" and "yulhidun." Al-ilhad (inclination, deviation) means turning away, and the one who is a mulhid is one who has turned away from the truth toward denial (al-taʿtil). So His saying ﴿yulhidun ilayhi﴾ means: they incline toward him.

And His saying ﴿yulhidun ilayhi﴾ means: they incline their speech toward him. Ibn Qutaybah said: "They gesture toward him." As for His saying ﴿foreign (aʿjami)﴾, the aʿjami is the one who does not speak Arabic clearly.

As for His saying ﴿and this is a clear Arabic tongue﴾, it means: a clear Arabic speech. The meaning of the verse is: how could he be taken from, when they do not speak Arabic clearly? It has been narrated that the man to whom they were pointing embraced Islam, and his Islam was good.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 104:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who do not believe in the signs of God, God will not guide them﴾. That is: God will not guide them to the truth. And He said in another place: ﴿And whoever believes in God, He will guide his heart﴾.

And His saying: ﴿And for them is a painful punishment﴾. That is: painful (ألِيم, alim), causing pain.

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Only those who do not believe in the signs of God fabricate lies, and it is they who are the liars.﴾ If someone says: He has said, "Only those who fabricate lies," so what is the meaning of His statement, "and it is they who are the liars"?

The answer to this is that His statement, "Only those who fabricate lies," is a report about the act of lying, while His statement, "and it is they who are the liars," is a permanent attribute (nu't lazim, an inherent descriptive attribute). Its meaning is that this is their character and their description. This is like a man who says to another, "You lied, and you are a liar," meaning: you lied in this statement, and lying is among your attributes.

In some musnads (hadith collections arranged by narrator) it is reported from Ya'la ibn al-Ashdaq, from Abdullah ibn Jarrad, that he said: "I said, 'O Messenger of God, does the believer commit adultery?' He said, 'That may happen.' I said, 'Does the believer steal?' He said, 'That may happen.' I said, 'Does the believer lie?' He said, 'No.' Then he recited His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Only those who do not believe in the signs of God fabricate lies.﴾" 

And from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may God be pleased with him) that he said: "Lying is incompatible with faith."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 106:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief﴾. The verse was revealed concerning 'Ammar ibn Yasir, may Allah be pleased with him. The polytheists seized him and compelled him to revile the Prophet, so he complied with them in some of what they said. Then he came to the Prophet, and the Prophet said to him: "What is behind you?" He replied: "Evil, O Messenger of Allah. The disbelievers did not leave me until I had spoken against you and mentioned their gods with good." He said: "How did you find your heart?" He said: "Content with faith." He said: "If they return, then return." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

The meaning of the verse is: "Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief, upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a painful punishment, except one who has been compelled while his heart is content with faith." ﴿But whoever opens his breast to disbelief﴾, then his ruling is what we have explained.

His saying ﴿opens﴾ means: he opened his heart to accept disbelief.

This is the commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 107.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿That is because they preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter﴾ means: they chose (ātharū) the life of this world over the Hereafter. And know that the believer may seek this world and seek the Hereafter, but none prefers this world over the Hereafter except the disbeliever. And His words: ﴿And that Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ means: He does not guide (lā yurshidu) the disbelieving people.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 108:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts, hearing, and sight Allah has sealed, and those are the heedless﴾. That is: heedless of what is intended for them.
The Exalted said: ﴿Without doubt, they will be the losers in the Hereafter.﴾ That is: truly, they are the ones who are cheated in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 110:

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Then indeed your Lord, for those who emigrated after they had been tried, then struggled and were patient — indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ The verse was revealed concerning a group of Muslims who had remained behind in Makkah, and the polytheists tortured them until they uttered the word of disbelief with their tongues. Among them were ʿAmmar, Khabbab, Suhayb, and others.

And His saying: ﴿after they had been tried﴾ means: they were tortured until they fell into trial (fitnah), and then after that they emigrated and joined the Prophet (ﷺ). And His saying: ﴿then struggled and were patient﴾ means: in striving (jihad) and in faith.

And His saying: ﴿indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ means: after their action which they did, namely giving the disbelievers some of what they wanted from them.

If someone says: If that was a concession (rukhsah), then would they not need forgiveness and mercy? The answer: it is possible that they did that before the concession was revealed.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 111:

The Most High's saying: ﴿On the Day when every soul comes pleading for itself﴾. If it is said: how does He say "pleading" (tujadil), when "every" (kull) has already been mentioned, and the word kull is masculine?

The answer to this: He returned the word kull to the feminine (meaning "soul"), so for this meaning the verb is feminine. This is like saying: "Every woman is standing," and what resembles this.

And His saying: ﴿pleading for itself﴾ means: disputing on its own behalf. Their disputing is their saying: "By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists," and their saying: "Our Lord, these are our associates whom we used to call upon besides You," and what resembles this from the statements mentioned in the Qur'an.

It has also been said: "pleading for itself" means: defending itself. It is related from Ka'b al-Ahbar (Ka'b al-Ahbar, the Jewish convert to Islam and transmitter of Israelite traditions) that he said: "Hell will emit a roar on the Day of Resurrection, and no angel brought near, nor any prophet sent, will remain without falling prostrate on his knees and saying: 'My soul! My soul!' until Abraham, the Friend of the Most Merciful, comes, and he says: 'My Lord, I want nothing but the salvation of my own soul.'" Ka'b said: "And it is in the Book of God the Most High: ﴿On the Day when every soul comes pleading for itself﴾."

It is also related that he said this in the presence of ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, and ʿUmar had said to him: "Tell us, remind us."

And His saying: ﴿and every soul will be paid in full for what it did, and they will not be wronged﴾ — its meaning is clear.

The Quranic verse on this passage: ﴿And Allah presents an example: a town that was secure and at ease⁠—﴾ and the rest of the verse.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (tafsir) on Surah 16, verse 112:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And Allah presents an example: a town that was secure and at ease﴾ – the verse. Most of the exegetes (ahl al-tafsir) said that the town here is Makkah. The words ﴿its provision comes to it abundantly from every place﴾ are the meaning of the Exalted's words: ﴿and provide for them from the fruits﴾.

His words ﴿but it denied the favours of Allah﴾: al-an'um is the plural of al-ni'mah (favour). His words ﴿so Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear﴾: He mentioned "tasting" because the intended meaning of "the garment of hunger and fear" is punishment, and it is fitting to say "taste" regarding punishment, as the Exalted said: ﴿Taste! Indeed you are the mighty, the noble﴾.

The meaning is that the punishment is renewed in its perception every hour, like tasting.

It is narrated that Allah the Exalted sent upon them famine for seven years until they ate the burnt food (al-ta'am al-muhtariqah) and al-'ilhiz, which is fur mixed with blood, until one of them would look at the sky and see something like smoke because of hunger.

﴿And fear﴾ is the fear of being killed, and of the raids of the Prophet.

The intended meaning of "the town" is its people, as in the Exalted's words: ﴿and ask the town﴾, and likewise His words ﴿secure﴾ mean its people were secure, and likewise "at ease."

There is another view regarding the verse: that it refers to every city of the disbelievers.

There is a third view regarding the verse: that it is Madinah, and the denial of its people of the favours of Allah is what they did after the Prophet, namely the killing of 'Uthman and what followed from matters; this is a weak view. As for the mention of the garment in the verse, it is because whoever goes hungry suffers emaciation, paleness and change that make his outward appearance worse than before; so that is made like a garment for his skin.

His words ﴿because of what they used to do﴾ mean: they used to disbelieve.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 113:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And there had certainly come to them a Messenger from among themselves﴾. That is, Muhammad (ﷺ). And His saying: ﴿from among themselves﴾ means: of their lineage. He is Muhammad son of ʿAbd Allah son of ʿAbd al-Muttalib son of Hashim son of ʿAbd Manaf son of Qusayy son of Kilab son of Murrah son of Kaʿb son of Lu'ayy son of Ghalib son of Fihr son of Malik son of al-Nadr son of Kinanah son of Khuzaymah son of Mudrikah son of Ilyas son of Mudar son of Nizar son of Maʿadd son of ʿAdnan.

And His saying: ﴿so they denied him﴾ means: they disbelieved in him. And His saying: ﴿so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers﴾ means: they were disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 114:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So eat of what Allah has provided for you, lawful and good, and be grateful for the favour of Allah, if it is Him that you worship﴾. We have already explained the meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 115:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He has only forbidden you carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah. But whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ The meaning of His saying ﴿neither desiring﴾ is: seeking it in order to strengthen himself for disobedience. ﴿Nor transgressing﴾ means: not exceeding the amount that was permitted to him for consumption. This is evidence that a sinner on a journey is not granted this concession (rukhsah).

As for His saying ﴿Indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 116:

His saying: ﴿And do not say, concerning what your tongues describe falsely﴾ means: concerning the description your tongues give to falsehood. And His saying: ﴿"This is lawful and this is unlawful"﴾ is meant to refer to what they had designated concerning the baḥīrah (a she-camel whose ear was slit and released), the sā'ibah (a free-roaming animal), the waṣīlah (a ewe that bore twins of alternating sexes), and the ḥām (a stallion camel released after siring a set number of offspring); they would declare these lawful for one people and forbid them to another. And His saying: ﴿so that you may fabricate against Allah falsehood﴾ means: so that you may invent falsehood against Allah. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who fabricate against Allah falsehood will not succeed﴾ means: they will not prosper.

Almighty Allah's words: ﴿A brief enjoyment, and for them there is a painful punishment﴾. That is: their life in this world is a brief enjoyment, ﴿and for them there is a painful punishment﴾, that is: agonizing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 118:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And to those who became Jews We prohibited what We have related to you before⟩. Its meaning: what He mentioned in Surah al-An'am, which is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And to those who became Jews We prohibited every animal with claws⟩. And His saying: ﴿And We did not wrong them⟩, meaning: We did not diminish anything of their rights. ﴿But they used to wrong themselves⟩, meaning: it is they who diminished their own rights.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 119:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then indeed your Lord, for those who did evil in ignorance⦁﴾. The people of knowledge said: Everyone who acts in disobedience, it is from the call of ignorance (jahala). His saying: ﴿Then they repented after that and reformed⦁﴾, reformation (salah) is a condition here, and its meaning is: steadfastness upon repentance. His saying: ﴿indeed your Lord, after it, is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful⦁﴾, i.e., after the deed from which they repented.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 120:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a community (ummah)﴾. There are several opinions concerning the meaning of "ummah." The best of these opinions is what Masruq related from Ibn Mas'ud, that it means a teacher of good, the one who is followed and taken as a leader (imam).

It is also narrated that Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said, after the death of Mu'adh ibn Jabal: "Mu'adh ibn Jabal was an ummah," and he meant this sense.

The second opinion: he was an ummah, that is, a leader (imam) of guidance. The third opinion: he was an ummah, that is, he was a believer in God while all other people were disbelievers.

And His words: ﴿devoutly obedient to God (qanitan lillah)﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: "obedient to God." Others said: "standing firm in obedience to God's commands." It was also said: "constantly devoted to worship."

His words: ﴿upright (hanifan)﴾, meaning sincere. It was also said: "steadfast upon the religion."

His words: ﴿and he was not of the polytheists﴾, meaning, he was not among those who worship idols. Some scholars of the meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: "He used to see that giving and withholding come from God."

His words, ﴿grateful for His blessings﴾, mean: for His blessings. His words, ﴿He chose him and guided him﴾, mean: He selected him and directed him. His words, ﴿to a straight path﴾, mean: to the religion of truth.

"His saying: ﴿And We gave him good in this world﴾. It was said: it is prophethood. It was said: it is the tongue of truthfulness (lisan al-sidq). It was said: it is the exalting of his mention because of his obedience to his Lord. It was said: it is the acceptance of him by all the adherents of the religions (milal). It was said: it is his hospitality and the people's supplication for him until the Day of Resurrection. And His saying: ﴿And indeed he, in the Hereafter, is among the righteous﴾, its meaning is apparent."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 123:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then We revealed to you: follow the religion of Abraham, a man of pure faith (hanif)﴾. This is evidence that it is permissible for the superior to follow the inferior. And His saying: ﴿And he was not of the polytheists﴾ is clear in meaning.

Some of the scholars of usul (the foundations of jurisprudence) have said: the Prophet was commanded to follow the law of Abraham except for what was abrogated in his law, by the evidence of this verse. It has been said otherwise, but the sound view is that he was commanded to follow his law in some matters, and that became a law for him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 124:

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the Sabbath was only made [binding] upon those who differed concerning it﴾. Its meaning: the Sabbath was only made a curse upon those who differed concerning it. His words "differed concerning it" mean: they opposed one another regarding it. Some of them said: "differed concerning it" means that some of them declared it forbidden and some of them declared it permitted, meaning the Sabbath.

Mujahid said: Allah, the Exalted, had commanded them to observe the Friday, but they refused, and they sought the Sabbath, so He imposed strictness upon them regarding it. Likewise, the Christians were commanded to observe the Friday, but they refused, and they sought Sunday (al-Ahad). Allah, the Exalted, gave the Friday to this Ummah, and they accepted it, and blessing was granted to them through it. There is a sound report on this subject, which we have explained earlier.

His statement: ﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ﴾. Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 125:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Call to the way of your Lord﴾: to the religion of your Lord. And His saying: ﴿with wisdom﴾: that is, with the Quran. It was also said: wisdom is knowing things in their proper ranks in terms of goodness and ugliness. It was also said: calling with wisdom is turning away from what is ugly toward what is good, on condition of knowledge.

And His saying: ﴿and good admonition﴾: admonition is calling to God by means of encouragement and warning. It was also said: good admonition is gentle, soft speech, without harshness or reproach.

And His saying: ﴿and argue with them in the way that is best﴾: that is, while turning away from their harm to you and enduring their offense. This was abrogated by the verse of the sword.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of those who are guided﴾: its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 126:

God the Exalted says: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished.﴾ Most of the people of tafsir (tafsir, Qur'anic exegesis) say that this verse was revealed concerning what the polytheists did to Hamzah and his companions. It is narrated: "The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by him, and his belly had been ripped open, his liver taken out, his private parts cut off and placed in his mouth. He saw a dreadful sight and said: 'If I gain power over them, I will mutilate seventy of them.' It is also narrated that the Companions said something close to this statement, so God the Exalted revealed this verse."

Zayd ibn Aslam and al-Dahhak said: the verse is Meccan, and it is not about Hamzah and his companions. The first view is the more sound.

As for His saying: ﴿But if you endure patiently, it is better for the patient.﴾ That is, if you pardon, ﴿it is better for the patient﴾, meaning: better for those who pardon. This pardon was realized in the case of Wahshi, the slayer of Hamzah, after he embraced Islam, and likewise this applies to every polytheist who embraced Islam.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 16, verse 127:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And be patient, and your patience is not but through Allah﴾, meaning: by the help of Allah. And His saying: ﴿And do not grieve over them﴾, meaning: do not grieve over their deeds and their refusal of Islam.

And His saying: ﴿And do not be in distress over what they plot﴾. It was read as "fī ḍayq" (in distress), and the meaning of the two readings is: let your chest not be constricted. ﴿Over what they plot﴾, meaning: what they associate (with Allah). It was also said: over the evil deeds they committed.

Almighty God's saying: ﴿Indeed, God is with those who are mindful of Him, and those who are doers of good.﴾ He means: those who guard against the prohibited things (ittaqaw al-manahi), and ﴿those who are doers of good﴾ through performing the obligatory duties (bi-ada' al-fara'id). And [His saying] ﴿with﴾ [means] with protection, support, and aid. And God knows best.
